meta.description: Report harassment anonymously, explore community safety data, and stay informed with HerSafe.

home.hero_subtitle: HerSafe lets you report harassment anonymously, see which areas your community marks safer, and help build a clearer, kinder map of the everyday.
home.mission_body: Most harassment goes unspoken because reporting feels exposing. HerSafe removes that cost — no names, no faces, no accusations. Just patterns the community can see and respond to.

about.title: About HerSafe
about.mission_body: To make everyday harassment visible as a pattern, without exposing any individual — so communities and institutions can respond to what the data shows.
about.vision_body: A world where reporting harassment costs nothing and prevents more of it.
about.privacy_body: No accounts are required to report. We never publish names, photos, or identifying details. Read our full Privacy Policy for details.
about.opensource_body: HerSafe's code is open for review, audit, and contribution.

support.title: What should I do after experiencing harassment?
support.intro: There's no single right way to respond — these are calm, practical starting points, not instructions.
support.step1_title: Move to a safer location if possible
support.step1_body: If you feel unsafe where you are, prioritize getting somewhere with other people, lighting, or a Safe Place nearby.
support.step2_body: A friend, family member, or colleague can help you feel less alone and support your next steps.
support.step3_title: Write down details while they're fresh
support.step3_body: Time, location, and what happened — in your own words, for your own reference. You never have to share this with anyone.
support.step4_title: Preserve any evidence you already have
support.step4_body: Screenshots, messages, or photos you already took are worth keeping safe. Don't feel pressured to gather more than you're comfortable with.
support.step5_title: Consider reporting to relevant authorities, if appropriate
support.step5_body: This is entirely your choice and on your timeline. HerSafe's own anonymous report is a separate, lower-stakes option that never requires this step.
support.step6_title: If you feel unwell or injured, seek medical care
support.step6_body: Physical and emotional reactions are normal and valid. It's okay to prioritize your body and mind first.
support.evidence1: Take screenshots immediately — messages can be deleted or edited later.
support.evidence2: Note the date, time, and platform or location for anything you save.
support.evidence3: Keep a backup copy somewhere separate from the original device if you can.
support.privacy1: You are never required to name anyone or share identifying details to get support.
support.privacy2: Be selective about who you tell and when — it's your information to share on your terms.
support.privacy3: If you use HerSafe's evidence links feature, double-check your Google Drive sharing settings first.
support.faq1_q: Do I have to report this to anyone?
support.faq1_a: No. Reporting — to HerSafe, to authorities, or to anyone else — is always your choice, not an obligation.
support.faq2_q: What if I'm not sure what happened counts as harassment?
support.faq2_a: If it made you feel unsafe or uncomfortable, it's valid to want support and information regardless of how it's categorized.
support.faq3_a: No — this is general, supportive information, not legal advice specific to any country. For legal questions, consider consulting a local lawyer or legal aid service.
support.emergency_note: If you're in immediate danger, contact emergency services first — see the numbers below.
